a:r.a:t: Vitamins E, K, and Other Lipid Quinones

p:cNvPr.descr: Structures of various isoprenoid compounds or derivatives. (a) Vitamin E: an antioxidant (labeled left). Beginning on the left, there are 2 ring structures bonded side by side. The left is a benzene ring. Beginning at the top carbon, C bonds up to CH3 and double bonds left to C, which bonds up to OH and down and left to C. C bonds down and left to CH3 and double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to CH3 and right and up to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds left to the initial carbon. This ring is bonded on the right to a tetrahydropyran ring (6-sided ring with an O) where the O is at the bottom. The C to the right of this is bonded right to 1 CH2 at the top and 1 CH3 at the bottom. CH2 bonds right to a long, straight chain of 12 carbons. Each carbon is part of CH2 except for the ones that bond up to CH3, which is every fourth carbon. The carbons are split into 3 groups of 4 by pink dotted lines bisecting the carbon bonds. (b) Below is Vitamin K1: a blood clotting cofactor (phylloquinone) (labeled left). The structure here is similar to that of vitamin E. The left ring is a benzene ring, bonded to nothing but the ring to its right, which has a single double bond on its right side. It is double bonded above and below to O. On its right, it is bonded to CH3 on top and CH2 on the bottom (adjacent carbons, not the same carbon). A dashed pink line bisects the bond between the ring and CH2, signaling the beginning of the chain. The chain consists of CH2 bonded right to CH, which double bonds right to C, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH2. Here there is another pink dashed line bisecting the bond. To the right of the bond there is a chain of 4 carbons, all of which are part of CH2 except for one, which bonds up to CH3. This section is in parentheses with a 2 outside it, indicating that it repeats again. To the right are 2 CH2 in a row, bonded right to CH, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH3. The chain is still divided up to 4-carbon groups. (c) Below is warfarin, a blood anticoagulant (labeled left). On the left side of the molecule is a benzene ring, bonded right to a 6-carbon ring with an incorporated O and one double bond at the bottom right. The O bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O. The same C bonds down and left to C, which bonds down and right to CH. C double bonds down and left to C, which bonds down to OH. The CH mentioned previously bonds right to a benzene ring and down and right to CH2, which bonds right to C. C double bonds down to O, then right to CH3.
